description: Each rating's average length is compared with the mean length over all individual films.

d.request: Find ratings whose average film length exceeds the overall mean length of all films, then among those, retain only ratings whose average length also exceeds the mean of that filtered group's average lengths, returning the mean of the final set's average lengths along with the average distances they sit above the overall mean and above the first-filter group's mean.
d.sql:
WITH overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(length) as overall_avg FROM film
),
first_filter AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(length) as avg_length
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
  HAVING AVG(length) > (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall_mean)
),
first_filter_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_length) as first_filter_avg FROM first_filter
),
second_filter AS (
  SELECT rating, avg_length
  FROM first_filter
  WHERE avg_length > (SELECT first_filter_avg FROM first_filter_mean)
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_length) as final_set_mean,
  AVG(avg_length - (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall_mean)) as avg_distance_above_overall_mean,
  AVG(avg_length - (SELECT first_filter_avg FROM first_filter_mean)) as avg_distance_above_first_filter_mean
FROM second_filter

b.request: For each film rating, calculate its average length (excluding NULLs); identify ratings with average length greater than the overall mean film length; from these, keep only ratings with average length greater than the mean of the first-cut ratings' average lengths; return the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, their average excess over the overall mean film length, and their average excess over the mean of the first-cut ratings' average lengths.
b.sql:
WITH film_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    rating,
    AVG(length) as avg_length
  FROM film
  WHERE length IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(length) as overall_avg
  FROM film
  WHERE length IS NOT NULL
),
first_cut AS (
  SELECT 
    fs.rating,
    fs.avg_length
  FROM film_stats fs
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
  WHERE fs.avg_length > om.overall_avg
),
first_cut_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_length) as first_cut_avg
  FROM first_cut
),
second_cut AS (
  SELECT 
    fc.rating,
    fc.avg_length
  FROM first_cut fc
  CROSS JOIN first_cut_mean fcm
  WHERE fc.avg_length > fcm.first_cut_avg
)
SELECT 
  AVG(sc.avg_length) as mean_remaining_avg_lengths,
  AVG(sc.avg_length - om.overall_avg) as avg_excess_over_overall_mean,
  AVG(sc.avg_length - fcm.first_cut_avg) as avg_excess_over_first_cut_mean
FROM second_cut sc
CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
CROSS JOIN first_cut_mean fcm
b.raw: For each film rating, calculate its average length (excluding NULLs); identify ratings with average length greater than the overall mean film length; from these, keep only ratings with average length greater than the mean of the first-cut ratings' average lengths; return the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, their average excess over the overall mean film length, and their average excess over the mean of the first-cut ratings' average lengths.

a.request: Compute each film `rating`'s average `length`, ignoring missing lengths. As the baseline, take the average length over all films, with each film counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above that baseline. Among those ratings, take the mean of their average lengths and keep only the ratings that are above that mean too. Return one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, and the mean amount by which they exceed the kept ratings' mean. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rating_avgs AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) as avg_length FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), baseline_calc AS (SELECT AVG(length) as baseline_avg FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL), above_baseline AS (SELECT ra.avg_length FROM rating_avgs ra, baseline_calc b WHERE ra.avg_length > b.baseline_avg), kept_mean_calc AS (SELECT AVG(avg_length) as kept_mean FROM above_baseline), final_kept AS (SELECT ab.avg_length FROM above_baseline ab, kept_mean_calc km WHERE ab.avg_length > km.kept_mean) SELECT AVG(avg_length) as mean_of_remaining, AVG(avg_length) - (SELECT baseline_avg FROM baseline_calc) as mean_excess_over_baseline, AVG(avg_length) - (SELECT kept_mean FROM kept_mean_calc) as mean_excess_over_kept_mean FROM final_kept

c.request: Which film ratings have an average `length` (ignoring missing lengths) that is longer than average? Of those ratings, keep only the ones that also run longer than the mean of their own average lengths. Give one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, how far on average they sit above that first average, and how far on average they sit above the mean of the ratings that passed the first cut. No rounding. Each rating's average length is compared with the mean length over all individual films.
c.sql: WITH film_avg AS (SELECT AVG(length) as overall_avg FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL), rating_avgs AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) as rating_avg FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), first_cut AS (SELECT rating, rating_avg FROM rating_avgs WHERE rating_avg > (SELECT overall_avg FROM film_avg)), first_cut_avg AS (SELECT AVG(rating_avg) as fc_avg FROM first_cut), second_cut AS (SELECT rating, rating_avg FROM first_cut WHERE rating_avg > (SELECT fc_avg FROM first_cut_avg)) SELECT AVG(rating_avg), AVG(rating_avg - (SELECT overall_avg FROM film_avg)), AVG(rating_avg - (SELECT fc_avg FROM first_cut_avg)) FROM second_cut
